figures.name: Jonah of Beth Asa
figures.description: Syriac priest from Beth Asa and brother of Brihishoʿ. Went to prison during a persecution to encourage future martyrs, then was arrested and martyred.

figures.name: Jonah of Hah
figures.description: Bishop of Hah in Tur Abdin, martyred at Apamea.

figures.name: Yazdanduht of Arbela
figures.description: Holy woman of Arbela (Adiabene) who in 345 took care of and buried 120 martyrs of Adiabene (111 priests and deacons; nine virgins).

figures.name: Yazdapnah, Bishop of Kashkar
figures.description: Bishop of Kashkar and contemporary of Patriarch Mar Emmeh and Rabban Theodore.

figures.name: Benjamin, Metropolitan of Edessa
figures.description: Metropolitan bishop of Edessa, professor of dogma, and commentator on the homilies of Gregory of Nazianzus and on the works of Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite.

figures.name: Yozadaq
figures.description: Monk and disciple of Rabban Bar ʿIdta and companion of Rabban Hormizd on Mount Resa. Built a monastery and corresponded about the works of Isaac of Nineveh.

figures.name: Zakka
figures.description: Disciple of Mar Mattai connected with the saints of Mosul. Successor of Mar Mattai, he inhabited a cell at the end of the valley of Mar Abraham.

figures.name: Zeʿora
figures.description: Stylite saint whose life was memorialized by John of Ephesus. Replaced his teacher on the pillar when the former retired. Travelled to Constantinople to advocate for the Miaphysite cause before Empress Theodora.

figures.name: Zayna of Tagrit
figures.description: Bishop and martyr whose cult in Tagrit rivaled that of Behnam and Sara at Mar Mattai. Son of Ator, a king, who became a monk and bishop.

figures.name: Basil of Samosata
figures.description: Monk at Qenneshrin and bishop of Samosata, the ancient Aramean city on the Euphrates.

figures.name: ʿAbdalʿaleq
figures.description: Syriac Christian deacon and martyr who was stoned to death.

figures.name: Abi
figures.description: Syriac saint featured in John of Ephesus' Lives of the Eastern Saints.

figures.name: ʿAbdishoʿ (companion of Berikhisho)
figures.description: Syriac Christian martyr who was killed alongside Berikhisho.

figures.name: ʿAbdishoʿ of Dasen
figures.description: Syriac monk from Dasen who trained in the monastery of Beth Sayare.

figures.name: Anton of Tagrit
figures.description: Syriac author from Tagrit (Tikrit), designated 'rhetor' and 'philoponos.' A monk from the family of Gurgin.

figures.name: Abel of Adiabene
figures.description: Aramean Christian saint from Adiabene, commemorated in Syriac hagiographic manuscripts.

figures.name: Aboursam
figures.description: Priest who died alongside Bishop Miles of Susa and the deacon Sinai.

figures.name: ʿAboushta of Adiabene
figures.description: Spiritual father from a village called Tallpna in the mountains of Adiabene.

figures.name: Abraham (companion of Maron)
figures.description: Syriac saint commemorated in John of Ephesus' Lives of the Eastern Saints alongside Maron.

figures.name: Abraham (companion of Addai)
figures.description: Syriac saint commemorated in John of Ephesus' Lives of the Eastern Saints alongside Addai.

figures.name: Abraham of Harran
figures.description: Syriac saint from Harran, the ancient Aramean city.

figures.name: Dionysios of Tel Mahre
figures.description: Syriac Orthodox Patriarch (818-845) and historian.

figures.name: Abraham of Nisibis
figures.description: Syriac saint from Nisibis, the Aramean city.

figures.name: Abraham I of Adiabene
figures.description: Early bishop of Adiabene, originally from Herda.

figures.name: Abraham II of Adiabene
figures.description: Bishop of Adiabene in the 4th century.

figures.name: Abraham the Priest
figures.description: Syriac priest featured in John of Ephesus' Lives of the Eastern Saints.

figures.name: Abraham the Recluse
figures.description: Syriac recluse saint featured in John of Ephesus' Lives of the Eastern Saints.

figures.name: Acacius of Aleppo
figures.description: Bishop of Aleppo venerated by the poet Balai.

figures.name: Aha of Adiabene (son of priest)
figures.description: Son of a priest from Arbela in Adiabene.

figures.name: Ahudemmeh
figures.description: Prominent East Syriac bishop and missionary.

figures.name: Ananias (Mardin)
figures.description: Syriac saint commemorated in a hagiographic manuscript from Mardin.

figures.name: Barhadbshabba of Mor Matay
figures.description: Syriac monk of the monastery of Mor Matay near Mosul.

figures.name: Nuhra
figures.description: Syriac saint whose name means 'light' in Syriac.

figures.name: Simeon of Samosata (pupil of Ephrem)
figures.description: Pupil of St. Ephrem from Samosata, the ancient Aramean city on the Euphrates.

figures.name: Papa, Bishop of Arzun
figures.description: Bishop of Arzun in the Aramean region.

figures.name: Paul the Interpreter
figures.description: Syriac commentator on the Psalms. Possibly Paul of Nisibis or Paul of Tella.

figures.name: Pethion (Catholicos)
figures.description: Catholicos of the Church of the East (731-740/741). Formed a favorable relationship with the Muslim governor Halid al-Qasri.

figures.name: Elijah of Harran
figures.description: Bishop of Salamya from Harran, the ancient Aramean city.

figures.name: Pethion of Dasen
figures.description: Monk and founder of a convent north of the Greater Zab.

figures.name: Peter of Antioch (bishop)
figures.description: Bishop of Antioch martyred under Emperor Maximinus.

figures.name: Peter of Antioch (patriarch)
figures.description: Patriarch of Antioch who reinforced connections with Alexandria and fought against what he considered heresies of Damian of Alexandria.

figures.name: Pinhas of Qardu
figures.description: Martyr from Qardu and disciple of Mar Awgin.

figures.name: Theodorus bar Zarudi
figures.description: Syriac scholar active in the 9th century.

figures.name: Mar Qardag
figures.description: Military saint and martyr from north of Arbela (Adiabene). Convert from a high-born Zoroastrian family. His teacher was Mar Abdisho.

figures.name: Qashish of Hah
figures.description: Monk from Hah in Tur Abdin. Went on pilgrimages and helped Empress Theodora build a hostel for Miaphysites.

figures.name: Qawma of Beth Garmai
figures.description: Monk and dendrite saint from Beth Garmai whose body did not decay.

figures.name: Qayyuma of Baz
figures.description: Monk who evangelized the region of Baz near Hakkari.

figures.name: Quna, Bishop of Edessa
figures.description: Bishop of Edessa who set the foundations for the new cathedral of Edessa, finished by his successor Saʿad.

figures.name: Simeon of Tagrit
figures.description: Syriac writer from Tagrit (Tikrit). Also known as Simeon bar ʿAmraye.

figures.name: Ruben of Qartmin
figures.description: Monk and perhaps stylite of the monastery of Qartmin in Tur Abdin.

figures.name: Saʿad, Bishop of Edessa
figures.description: Bishop of Edessa who completed the cathedral begun by his predecessor Quna.

figures.name: Saba Pirgushnasp
figures.description: Child of the governor of Beth ʿArabaye martyred under Shapur II at the age of 12.

figures.name: Sabbatius
figures.description: Solitary monk who lived near the banks of the Euphrates.

figures.name: Shabra of Midyat
figures.description: Child saint commemorated near Midyat in Tur Abdin.

figures.name: David bar Paulos
figures.description: Syriac author from Beth Rabban.

figures.name: Samuel of Qartmin
figures.description: From Eshtin near Mardin. Founded the monastery of Qartmin (Mor Gabriel) with the help of an angel. Performed numerous miracles and ended a plague over Hah.

figures.name: Cyriacus, Patriarch of Antioch
figures.description: Patriarch of Antioch (793-817) from Tagrit. Monk of the Monastery of Estona near Kallinikos on the Euphrates. Held at least five synods.

figures.name: Shapor, Bishop of Niqator
figures.description: Bishop of Niqator (Awana) martyred under Shapur II alongside Isaac, bishop of Karka.

figures.name: Sharbel of Edessa
figures.description: Former pagan priest of Edessa who converted to Christianity. Martyred under Emperor Trajan alongside his sister Babai. Contemporary of Bishop Barsamya.

figures.name: Sabrishoʿ of Tagrit
figures.description: Monk who founded the monastery of the martyrs near Tagrit. His monks took refuge in a village during the Muslim conquest.

figures.name: Athanos the Malphono
figures.description: Syriac teacher (malphono) active in the early 9th century.

figures.name: Sergius of Huzri
figures.description: Deacon of Huzri who may also have been a writer.

figures.name: Sergius of Tella
figures.description: Successor of Jacob Baradaeus from Tella. Accompanied his teacher to Constantinople. Eventually ordained Miaphysite bishop of Antioch.

figures.name: Sergius of the Barren Mountain
figures.description: Monk who founded the Suspended Monastery (Dayr al-Muʿallaq) on the Barren Mountain. It became the residence of the bishops of Balad.

figures.name: Sergius of Zuqnin
figures.description: Monk at the monastery of Zuqnin, possibly identified with Sergius of Qenneshrin.

figures.name: Severus the Wonderworker
figures.description: Bishop of Samosata and brother of Patriarch Athanasius the Camel-Driver. Known for chasing away demons. Accompanied his brother to meet Heraclius.

figures.name: Severus of Kafar Ze
figures.description: Superior of the monastery of Qartmin, mentioned in the Life of Samuel of Qartmin.

figures.name: Severus the Mathematician
figures.description: Astronomer from Nisibis who became bishop of Qenneshrin in 630.

figures.name: Silvanus of Edessa
figures.description: The 26th bishop of Edessa.

figures.name: Simeon of Kfar-ʿAbdin
figures.description: Monk from Edessa who went to Samosata on the Euphrates. Shared his cave with an anchorite named Elijah and performed many miracles.

figures.name: Simeon, Bishop of Edessa
figures.description: Bishop of Edessa, succeeded by Gabriel.

figures.name: Simeon (martyr under Yazdgerd II)
figures.description: Martyr under Yazdgerd II, commemorated with Shapor bishop of Niqator, Isaac bishop of Karka, Maʿna, and Abraham.

figures.name: Simeon of Qartmin
figures.description: Second founder and second abbot of the monastery of Qartmin (Mor Gabriel). Healed as a youth by Samuel of Qartmin. Blessed Rabbula of Edessa.

figures.name: Simeon of Dara
figures.description: Bishop of Dara who participated in the synod of Mantzikert that sealed union with the Armenian church.

figures.name: Simeon of Papo
figures.description: Superior of Qartmin who opened the eyes of a blind man before Shah Khusro.

figures.name: Simeon of Qarqafto
figures.description: Builder of the Qarqaphto (The Skull) Monastery between Reshʿayna and Magdal in the high Gazira.

figures.name: Simeon the Stylite the Younger
figures.description: From Antioch, child of John and Martha. Showed signs of holiness as an infant. Lived on a column on the Wonderful Mountain.

figures.name: Shirin of Beth Zadoq
figures.description: Martyr from Beth Zadoq. When she learned of 12000 martyrs under Yazdegerd II, she took herself and her children before the governor and confessed her faith. She and her children were decapitated.

figures.name: Shirin of Karka d-Beth Slokh
figures.description: Born in Karka d-Beth Slokh to a Zoroastrian family, converted to Christianity. Faced great hardship, was imprisoned and executed.

figures.name: Shlemun the Mourner
figures.description: Bishop of Hadita on the Tigris. Converted Muslims, opposed election of Catholicos Timothy I in 780. Died at monastery of Mar Ahrun near Balad.

figures.name: Shmona of Edessa
figures.description: Aramean martyr killed in Edessa during the Diocletian persecution alongside Gourya. Subject of great devotion in Edessa.

figures.name: Lazarus bar Sobtho
figures.description: Bishop of Baghdad and author of an Anaphora as well as liturgical and theological works.

figures.name: Stratonike (sister of Mar Awgin)
figures.description: Sister of Mar Awgin and Thecla. Mentioned in the Hymns on the Holy Women.

figures.name: Tahmazgerd of Kirkuk
figures.description: Executioner converted upon seeing the example of the martyrs of Kirkuk including Shirin. Crucified upside down. A church of Mar Tahmasgard exists in Kirkuk.

figures.name: Talia
figures.description: Child martyr at age two. Son of Sabellius and Shapira. Tried and tortured multiple times. A shrine at Romaniya was built for him.

figures.name: Tarbo
figures.description: Sister of Simeon Bar Sabbaʿe. After Simeon's execution, she was accused of witchcraft by the wife of Shapur. She and her servant were tortured and cut into pieces.

figures.name: John of Qartmin
figures.description: Noted paleographer from the monastery of Qartmin (also called John of Beth Sbirino) who reestablished the use of estrangelo writing.

figures.name: John the Nazarite
figures.description: Monk of Tur ʿAbdin, possibly the 'perfect Nazarite' mentioned by John of Ephesus. From Zuqnin near Amida, forced to leave his cave due to Chalcedonian aggression.

figures.name: John of Edessa (Priest)
figures.description: Priest from Edessa who nourished 12 holy men in a cave. Became friends with Paul of Edessa. Travelled to Sinai and Jerusalem. Lived in the time of Bishop Rabbula.

figures.name: Jacob of Adiabene
figures.description: Zealot priest from Adiabene arrested with John bar Maryam, Bishop of Arbela, during the time of Shapur. Decapitated at Beth Lapat.

figures.name: John bar Maryam
figures.description: Bishop of Arbela arrested with Jacob the zealot. Sent to Shapur, flogged, and decapitated.

figures.name: Job of Adiabene
figures.description: Great teacher (doctor) of the Syriac church from Adiabene.

figures.name: Joseph (disciple of Narsai)
figures.description: Disciple of Narsai, martyred together in Beth Garmai.

figures.name: Joseph, Patriarch of Antioch
figures.description: Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch.

figures.name: Joseph of Arbela
figures.description: Priest and martyr of Arbela in Adiabene.

figures.name: Julian, Patriarch of Antioch
figures.description: Patriarch of Antioch and monk of Qenneshrin. Wrote against Sergius of Armenia.

figures.name: Justina of Antioch
figures.description: Martyr from Antioch who died alongside Cyprian under Emperor Diocletian.

figures.name: Karkus of Antioch
figures.description: Successor of Ignatius in Antioch and fourth bishop of the city.

figures.name: Lawrence and Agrippa
figures.description: Companions and martyrs under Diocletian. Agrippa was a prefect of Syria who converted to the faith in Mesopotamia.

figures.name: Lazarus the Confessor
figures.description: Possibly a monk of Qartmin commemorated for martyrdom under a Persian general.

figures.name: Sultan Mahduk
figures.description: Martyr of Tur Berʿain in Beth Garmai, commemorated with her brothers Mirnarsai and Adorparwa.

figures.name: Maʿin
figures.description: General of Shapur II who converted to Christianity after witnessing the martyrdom of Dodo. Built 69 places of worship around Sinjar. Died at age 114 in a monastery near Europos.

figures.name: Cyriacus, Metropolitan of Tur ʿAbdin
figures.description: Metropolitan of Tur ʿAbdin in the 8th century.

figures.name: Malke
figures.description: Monk and nephew of Mar Awgin (son of his sister Rebecca). Joined his uncle on Mount Izla. Built a monastery near Ankah near Midyat and performed miracles.

figures.name: Mamas of Beth Sloth
figures.description: Martyr of Beth Sloth.

figures.name: Mamelhta of Beth Garmai
figures.description: Virgin and martyr from Beth Garmai.

figures.name: Maʿna
figures.description: Martyr killed under Yazdgerd II, connected to the group of Shapor of Niqator and Isaac of Karka d-Beth Slokh.

figures.name: Mari the Apostle
figures.description: Apostle to Mesopotamia ordained by Addai to establish Christian communities in the royal cities of the Parthians.

figures.name: Lazarus of Beth Qandasa
figures.description: Monk on the Holy Mountain of Edessa, scholar, and author of a commentary on the Pauline Epistles.

figures.name: Mary (daughter of the covenant, Adiabene)
figures.description: Daughter of the covenant martyred with Thecla in Adiabene.

figures.name: Mary of Tell Salila
figures.description: Martyr from the village of Tell Salila. Sister of the priest Jacob. Martyred at Tel Dara under Shapur.

figures.name: Marina
figures.description: Disguised herself as a man (Marinos) to enter a monastery with her father. Expelled after false accusation, miraculously nursed a baby. Venerated especially by Maronites.

figures.name: Maron of ʿAyn Ward
figures.description: Superior of the monastery of Qartmin mentioned in the life of Samuel of Qartmin. Baptized 2000 people in Mesopotamia.

figures.name: Martha (daughter of the covenant, Adiabene)
figures.description: Daughter of the covenant martyred with Thecla in Adiabene.

figures.name: Mar Mattai
figures.description: Born near Amida (Diyarbakir). Became a monk and fled persecution to the Mountain of Alpep northwest of Mosul, where he founded the famous monastery of Mor Mattai.

figures.name: Michael the Companion of Angels
figures.description: Monk linked to Mar Awgin. In some traditions the hagiographer of the Life of Awgin. Commemorated with other monastic founders in Mesopotamia.

figures.name: Michael of Tarʿil
figures.description: Disciple of Sabrishoʿ of Beth Qoqa. Commemorated at the monastery of Mar Mikhaʾil of Tarʿil in Adiabene.

figures.name: Michael of Mardin
figures.description: Martyred with his sister outside the gate of Mardin at the Monastery of the Fish (or Monastery of the Column).

figures.name: Micah of Nuhadra
figures.description: Founder of a monastery or church in the village of Alqosh, north of Mosul.

figures.name: Mihrnarsai
figures.description: Martyr of Tur Berʿain in Beth Garmai, commemorated with his brother Adorparwa and sister Sultan Mahduk.

figures.name: Miles of Tel Hesh
figures.description: Healed by the monk Daniel the Doctor. Consecrated bishop of Tel Hesh and stoned to death under Shapur.

figures.name: Moses of Beth Sayyare
figures.description: Helped restore the monastery of Beth Sayyare founded by Mar Abraham, a disciple of Mar Awgin.

figures.name: Mqadashta
figures.description: Sister of Tarbo and Catholicos Simeon bar Sabbaʿe. Martyred after her brother.

figures.name: George of Bʿeltan
figures.description: Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch (758-789). Monk of Qenneshrin who convoked the synod of Kafar Nubu.

figures.name: Narsai, Bishop of Sharqart
figures.description: Bishop of Sharqart and martyr of Beth Garmai, alongside his disciple Joseph.

figures.name: Narsai, son of the covenant
figures.description: Monk and martyr from Beth Garmai. Decapitated with his disciple Joseph.

figures.name: Longinus
figures.description: Ascetic who baptized Bassus and Suzanna, converts from Zoroastrianism. Commemorated as a martyr with them.

figures.name: Jacob of Beth Garmai
figures.description: Monk, visionary, and chanter from Beth Garmai. Took over a monastery founded by Ishoʿyahb which came to be named after him.

figures.name: Jacob, Bishop of Phesilta
figures.description: Disciple of Jacob Baradaeus who became bishop of the monastery of Phesilta.

figures.name: Jacob the Recluse (of Seert)
figures.description: Disciple of Abraham of Kashkar who co-founded a monastery near Siirt and Arzun in the Bohtan region.

figures.name: Jacob the Recluse (of Salah)
figures.description: Fled to Egypt during persecution of Julian, then headed east to Mesopotamia. Built a monastery at Salah in Tur ʿAbdin.

figures.name: Phocas of Edessa
figures.description: Syriac scholar from Edessa, also known as Phocas bar Sergius of Edessa.

figures.name: Jacob of Beth Naggare
figures.description: Priest of Beth Naggare near Adiabene martyred with the deacon Azad during the persecution of Shapur II.

figures.name: Jacob the Priest (of Tell Salila)
figures.description: Priest from the village of Tell Salila, martyred with his sister Mary during the reign of Shapur.

figures.name: John the Doctor
figures.description: Syriac doctor (physician/scholar).

figures.name: John bar ʿAbdun
figures.description: Syriac Orthodox Patriarch (1004-1033). Accused of attracting Chalcedonians, brought to Constantinople, slapped in Hagia Sophia by the Melkite Bishop of Melitene. Died in exile in Thrace and honored as a martyr.

figures.name: John the Blue
figures.description: Bishop of Hirta (al-Hira).

figures.name: John the Egyptian (Mount Qardu)
figures.description: Student of Mar Awgin who lived as a solitary on Mount Qardu. Converted pagans and built a monastery called Hlahlaḥ which was renamed after him.

figures.name: John the Camel-Driver
figures.description: Syriac bishop of the Egyptian diaspora captured by Bedouins. Found singing Syriac chants among Arab camel drivers. Recognized by Maran Zha, bishop of Hadita on the Tigris.

figures.name: John of Harran
figures.description: One of fifty Miaphysite bishops exiled under Justin I in 518. Bishop of Harran.

figures.name: John of Kafar Sania
figures.description: Martyr who died under Maximinus Hercules.

figures.name: John of Kashkar
figures.description: Born in the region of Kashkar. After a series of abductions, returned to the monastery of ʿAyn Deqla.

figures.name: John of Kfone
figures.description: Disciple of Mar Awgin. His monastery was found south of Zaz in Tur ʿAbdin.

figures.name: John Psaltes
figures.description: Mentioned in the Life of Samuel of Qartmin. A vision revealed to him the presence of relics at Hrbat Tuta.
